assessment.reason: The reconstructed view of src/go/internal/cellfill/cellfill.go declares one helper, `func AdmitSeatDecl(decl json.RawMessage, fill string, want cellmethod.Role, method cellmethod.View, refusal SeatRefusal) (SeatDecl, error)`, which applies OnlyKeys at the top object ("fill", "cognition") and at the nested cognition object ("provider", "model"), StrictDecodes into the shared SeatDecl{Fill, Cognition}, then refuses `method.Empty()` and `method.Role != want`. In the view of cdspatch.go, Factory calls `cellfill.AdmitSeatDecl(decl, Fill, cellmethod.RoleConstructive, method, cellfill.SeatRefusal{...})`; in cdsassess.go, Factory calls the same helper with `cellmethod.RoleAdversarial`. Both return their zero Constructed value plus the helper's error unchanged.

assessment.reason: Reading the full reconstructed views of cdspatch.go and cdsassess.go, neither contains `func exactShape` — both copies were deleted (the diff removes each, and the post-application files show no such symbol anywhere). Neither package declares a Decl type for the {fill, cognition} shape any more: that shape is declared once, as cellfill.SeatDecl. Zero copies satisfies the 'only one' bound, since the criterion's stated route is that the grep must find no exactShape in either file.

assessment.reason: The refusal texts are preserved byte-for-byte through the helper's format strings: `fmt.Errorf("fill %q: %s", fill, refusal.NoMethodology)` with NoMethodology = "a patch alpha needs the cell's methodology, and this cell declares none" / "an assessing beta needs the cell's methodology, and this cell declares none", and `fmt.Errorf("fill %q: %s, got %q", fill, refusal.WrongRole, method.Role)` with WrongRole = "a producing seat takes the constructive projection" / "an assessing seat takes the adversarial projection" — identical to the deleted inline literals. The shape refusals keep their `where` labels: OnlyKeys(decl, fill, ...) yields "cds.patch"/"cds.assess" and fill+".cognition" yields "cds.patch.cognition"/"cds.assess.cognition", each still wrapped `fill %q: %w`, and the check order (top keys, nested keys, StrictDecode, empty projection, role) is unchanged. The only test file touched is cellfill_test.go and every hunk in it is purely additive — three new tests over the helper, no existing assertion deleted, relaxed or made unreachable; no cdspatch or cdsassess test was modified. check:project-verify passed all four steps, including cdspatch, cdsassess and cellfill.
